entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
[3] The petitioner initially filed an application under Section 10(2) of the Petroleum and Minerals (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962 before the learned Additional District Judge, Sepahijala District,
Bishalgarh being dissatisfied with the amount of compensation determined by the Competent Authority and prayed for determination of compensation at 10% of the land value for the right of user of land.

entities.text: Petroleum and Minerals (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text:
Additional District Judge, Sepahijala District,
Bishalgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim was contested by the respondents by filing written statement inter alia alleging that the case was not maintainable as the same was barred by limitation.
They further stated that the compensation determined by the Competent Authority was just, proper and reasonable.

[4] After hearing the learned counsel for the respective parties, the following issues were framed :
"(i) Whether the case is maintainable in its present form and nature?
(ii) Whether the case is barred by Law of Limitation?
(iii) Whether the instant case is bad for non-joinder and mis- joinder of parties?
(iv) Whether the award/order passed by the respondent No.4 in respect of determination of the rate of compensation is/was just, proper and reasonable?

The Oil And Natural Gas Corporation And ... vs Sri Sukumar Debbarma on 9 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21435241/
1 (v) Whether the petitioner is entitled to get any relief as sought for?
(vi) To what relief or relieves claimant is entitled?"
[5] To establish the claim the petitioner adduced his oral evidence and exhibited the documents.

entities.text: Oil And Natural Gas Corporation And ... vs Sri Sukumar Debbarma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, Sri Uttam Mandal was examined as OPW-1 on behalf of the Competent Authority and also exhibited the documents.
One witness Sri Shakti Jamatia was also examined as OPW-2 on behalf of the respondents No.1 to 3, however, no document was exhibited by OPW-2.

[6] The learned Additional District Judge after framing the issues and after perusing the documents on record enhanced the compensation of Rs.10,47,600/- as business loss and compensation of Rs.3,000/- for acquired land and at the rate of 6% interest per annum after expiry of one month of the date of judgment.
The learned Judge further observed that the pipeline was laid under the land of the petitioner or the notification was issued in the year 2012.

Therefore, in the absence of any other document, at least the land value appearing in [Exbt.3] could be considered for assessing the value of the land at the relevant time and the same must have been increased over the value appearing in [Exbt.3].
Therefore, it was prima facie assessed that the value of the land at the relevant time was approximately 1 lac per kani.

[7] Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment of the learned Additional District Judge, the petitioner filed this instant petition seeking the following reliefs :
(i) Issue a Rule calling upon the respondent to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree passed on 22.09.2022 and 23.09.2022 respectively in Civil Misc (PMP) No.21 of 2014 between Sri Sukumar Debbarma, claimant petitioner and the Oil & Natural Gas Corporation Limited and 3 others, opposite parties (Annexure-1 supra) shall not be interfered with/quashed/set aside insofar as the fixing of liability for making the payment of compensation upon the petitioner ONGC and also to show cause as to why this Hon'ble Court shall not pass such further order or orders as may be deemed to be fit and proper;
(ii) Call for records and stay of the operation of impugned judgment and decree dated 22.09.2022 AND (iii) After hearing the parties be pleased to make the Rule absolute in terms of (i)
above."
[8] Mr. Ranjit Dasgupta, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contends that the learned Additional District Judge committed an error in passing the impugned judgment.
The learned Judge without answering the issues No.1 & 3 came to the conclusion and enhanced the compensation in favour of the claimant.

Consequently, he prays for setting aside of the impugned judgment dated 22.09.2022 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Sepahijala District Bishalgarh in Case No. Civil Misc.(PMP) 21 of 2014.

sentences.text: [9] It is seen from the record that mere indication of the court below that the issue Nos.1 and 3 have been decided and answered in earlier round of litigation by way of judgment dated 20.08.2021, is not sufficient.
The court below ought to have either reiterated the order or it could have dealt afresh and indicated the findings since nothing is elicited with regard to issues No.1 and 3.
This Court expresses its concern with regard to the manner in which the order is passed.
Hence, the instant petition is allowed and the matter is remanded back to the court below for deciding the matter afresh.
The court below shall pass a speaking order with regard to issue Nos.1 and 3 are concerned by giving an opportunity to both sides.

This exercise shall be completed within a period of 2 months from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and it is needless to mention that both the parties shall cooperate with the proceedings.
The other issues and remaining part of the judgment will remain the same.
[10] The civil revision petition is allowed to the extent indicated above.
Pending application(s), if any, also stands disposed of.
